name: LifeStance Health
one_liner: In-person and video therapy and psychiatry from a large US group practice in 33 states, mostly billed to your insurance.
best_for: People who want to see a therapist or psychiatrist in person, with video as an option
People with commercial insurance who want in-network care
Families looking for care for children and teens as well as adults
People who want therapy and medication management in the same practice
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People in states where LifeStance has no clinicians
People who need inpatient, residential or intensive programs
Self-pay patients who want a clear published price up front
short_description: A large outpatient group practice offering in-person and video therapy and psychiatry for all ages in 33 US states.
long_description: LifeStance Health is a US outpatient mental health company; it and its supported practices report more than 550 centers in 33 states. You choose a psychologist, therapist, psychiatrist or psychiatric nurse practitioner from its directory and meet in person or by video (telehealth clinicians must be licensed in the state you are in). It is in network with many commercial plans; self-pay estimates vary by state, for example $210 to $432 for a psychiatry visit, and uninsured patients can ask for a Good Faith Estimate. In April 2026 LifeStance released its own analysis of about 180,000 patients reporting that most improved on PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores, but this is a company report, not a peer-reviewed or controlled study. Clinical records are covered by its HIPAA notice; in a class action over Meta and Google tracking pixels on its website (2020 to 2023), it settled for $3 million without admitting wrongdoing and agreed to stop using those tracking tools.
patient_summary: You search LifeStance's directory for a therapist or psychiatrist near you, then see them in an office or by video. Most people pay their insurance copay; self-pay rates vary by state and are quoted by your local office (psychiatry visits run roughly $210 to $432).

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance; self-pay about $210–$432/session for psychiatry (varies by state)
pricing.notes: Self-pay rates are estimates set by state and location; LifeStance state pages from October 2024 list therapy at $213–$522 per visit in Ohio and $204–$375 in Oregon. Estimates exclude deductibles and coinsurance; uninsured patients can request a Good Faith Estimate. Call the local office for an exact price.

privacy.notes: Says it does not sell personal information, but its website policy describes marketing cookies for personalized ads elsewhere; settled a $3M class action (no admission) over Meta and Google pixels on its site from 2020 to 2023. Clinical records fall under its HIPAA notice.

seo.title: LifeStance Health: Therapy & Psychiatry | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: LifeStance Health has 550+ mental health clinics across 33 states. In-person and telehealth therapy and psychiatry. Most insurance accepted.

faqs.q: Does LifeStance Health accept my insurance?
faqs.a: LifeStance accepts most major commercial insurance plans including Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, United Healthcare, and many others. Coverage varies by location and plan. Contact your local LifeStance office or check their website to verify your specific insurance is accepted.

faqs.q: How quickly can I get an appointment at LifeStance?
faqs.a: Most patients can schedule appointments within 1-2 weeks, faster than many traditional practices. Wait times vary by location, clinician specialty, and appointment type. New patient evaluations may have longer wait times than follow-ups.

faqs.q: Does LifeStance offer both in-person and virtual appointments?
faqs.a: Yes, LifeStance offers both in-person appointments at their 550+ clinic locations and telehealth video appointments. Many patients use a hybrid approach—some sessions in-person, others virtual. Virtual availability depends on your state and provider licensing.

LifeStance treats anxiety, depression, ADHD, bipolar disorder, PTSD, OCD, eating disorders, and other mental health conditions. Services include therapy, psychiatry, and medication management for children, teens, and adults. Specialty services vary by location.

primary_uses: Child and adolescent mental health care
Psychological testing and assessment where offered
TMS for treatment-resistant depression at some locations

availability.note: In-person and telehealth care in 33 US states only; LifeStance reports more than 550 centers.
